subject: wantarray in a VOID-context string eval reports scalar (op/wantarray.t) — narrower than not-supported.md claimed; gated on the CLAUDE.md §8 VOID_CTX regression
description:
FOUND s319 triaging near-green suite files (task #150's list).

The blessed not-supported.md section "Context propagation into string eval" said
wantarray() inside a string eval cannot detect its calling context AT ALL.  That
is WRONG, measured (probe s319/pr-wa.pl):

  my $c = q{ $q = (defined wantarray) ? (wantarray ? 'A' : 'S') : 'V' };
  eval $c;              perl V   PCL S    <-- the ONLY divergence
  my $s = eval $c;      perl S   PCL S    correct
  my @l = eval $c;      perl A   PCL A    correct

Scalar and list work because *wantarray* is a CL dynamic variable and (load ...)
inherits whatever binding is in scope at the call site; the aassign / scalar
assign already establish the right one.  VOID is wrong because nothing binds
*wantarray* to :void at a void-context call site, so the eval sees the ambient
NIL (= scalar).

Confirmed by emission: `./pl2cl` on the three call sites emits a bare
(p-eval $c (list ...)) for ALL THREE -- no (let ((*wantarray* ...)) ...) wrapper
anywhere.  So the fix is to bind :void at void call sites, not to build the
AST-annotation machinery the old doc text pointed at.

not-supported.md CORRECTED in the same commit (it now carries the measured
three-row table and marks this a fix target, not a limitation).

SCOREBOARD: t/op/wantarray.t is 27/1 vs perl 28/0 -- this one row is the whole
gap.  NOT registered in perl-suite-expected.tsv: it is a fix target (CLAUDE.md
4), not a blessed limitation.

DO NOT START THIS YET: CLAUDE.md §8 says the VOID_CTX sub-body wrap in
_process_expression_statement is too broad and that regression must be fixed
BEFORE any further wantarray work.  Sequence: §8 regression -> this.

Related: #60 (the void-wrap hoist, wa_void_active) is where void-ness is already
known at emission time -- start there when picking this up.
